value.rationale: The exchange-symmetric apparent-competition equality is a natural excluded boundary of a recent global three-species classification. The new all-positive-data fate theorem resolves whether predator persistence can depend singularly on an infinitesimal prey composition imbalance. A finite, exact logarithmic transient-competition penalty independently quantifies the effect and diverges near the unstable balanced state; it does not depend on the predator uptake or total initial biomass. These are motivated structural results, not an arbitrary sample or a reformulation of the published generic cases.
